items.purity: Iron (99.9 wt.%), niobium (99.7 wt.%) and titanium (99.9 wt.%)
items.quote: Iron (99.9 wt.%), niobium (99.7 wt.%) and titanium (99.9 wt.%) were used as staring materials. Bulk buttons were prepared from pure elements by arc melting under an argon atmosphere and in a water-cooled copper crucible. Titanium was used as an oxygen getter during the melting process. Each alloy button was melted for six times in order to ensure homogeneity.
items.synthesis: Bulk buttons were prepared from pure elements by arc melting under an argon atmosphere and in a water-cooled copper crucible.

items.quote: Fig. 1(d) shows the three-phase microstructure (FeNb + FeTi + Fe2 (Nb, Ti)) of the Fe50 Nb24 Ti26 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1100 ◦ C for 30 days, where the FeNb phase, FeTi phase and Fe2 (Nb, Ti) phase are white, black and gray, respectively.

items.label: Fe85 Nb12 Ti3 (at.%)
items.quote: A two-phase equilibrium (Fe2 (Nb, Ti) + ␥Fe) was found in the Fe85 Nb12 Ti3 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1200 ◦ C for 15 days (Fig. 1(e)), and the Fe2 (Nb, Ti) phase evenly distribute in the matrix of the ␥Fe phase, and the XRD results are shown in Fig. 2(b), where the characteristic peaks of Fe2 (Nb, Ti) and ␥Fe phases are distinguished by different symbols.

items.label: Fe37 Nb35 Ti28 (at.%)
items.quote: In the Fe37 Nb35 Ti28 (at.%) alloy quenched from 1100 ◦ C for 30 days, the three-phase microstructure (FeNb + FeTi + (Nb, ␤Ti)) was observed (Fig. 1(c)) and substantiated by the XRD result as shown in Fig. 2(a), where the characteristic peaks of the FeNb, FeTi and (Nb, ␤Ti) phases are well marked by different symbols.

The specimens were annealed at 1200 ◦ C, 1100 ◦ C and 1000 ◦ C, respectively. The time of the heat treatment varied from several hours to 60 days depending on the temperature and composition of the specimen. At the end of the heat treatment, the specimens were quenched into ice water.

The Fe30 Nb50 Ti20 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1200 ◦ C for 15 days was found to be located in the threephase region (FeNb + FeTi + (Nb, ␤Ti)), as shown in Fig. 1(f), where the FeTi and (Nb, ␤Ti) phases distribute in the matrix of the FeNb phase.

items.applies_to: Fe22 Nb18 Ti60 (at.%) alloy and Fe30 Nb10 Ti60 (at.%) alloy
items.quote: The two-phase equilibrium microstructure of the (FeTi + (Nb, ␤Ti)) was identified in the Fe22 Nb18 Ti60 (at.%) alloy and Fe30 Nb10 Ti60 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1000 ◦ C for 60 days, as indicated in Fig. 1(a) and (b), where the FeTi phase and (Nb, ␤Ti) phase are gray and white, respectively.

Fig. 1(d) shows the three-phase microstructure (FeNb + FeTi + Fe2 (Nb, Ti)) of the Fe50 Nb24 Ti26 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1100 ◦ C for 30 days, where the FeNb phase, FeTi phase and Fe2 (Nb, Ti) phase are white, black and gray, respectively.

In the Fe37 Nb35 Ti28 (at.%) alloy quenched from 1100 ◦ C for 30 days, the three-phase microstructure (FeNb + FeTi + (Nb, ␤Ti)) was observed (Fig. 1(c)) and substantiated by the XRD result as shown in Fig. 2(a), where the characteristic peaks of the FeNb, FeTi and (Nb, ␤Ti) phases are well marked by different symbols.

A two-phase equilibrium (Fe2 (Nb, Ti) + ␥Fe) was found in the Fe85 Nb12 Ti3 (at.%) alloy annealed at 1200 ◦ C for 15 days (Fig. 1(e)), and the Fe2 (Nb, Ti) phase evenly distribute in the matrix of the ␥Fe phase, and the XRD results are shown in Fig. 2(b), where the characteristic peaks of Fe2 (Nb, Ti) and ␥Fe phases are distinguished by different symbols.
